content:
eli: heads-up — I sketched a small proposal for a new canary slice behavior that should reduce cross-cohort leakage when we have header overrides

samira: tl;dr?

eli: idea: prefer deterministic hash -> header override -> cookie stickiness, but only if the header is in an allowlist per-tenant. if header present and allowed, use header-based split; otherwise fall back to hash(cookie or client id). prevents accidental dev headers from hijacking canaries.

ken: hmm — why header allowlist over explicit header deny? feels like allowlist is safer for onboarding new routes but more config overhead.

eli: because we need explicit consent for owners who want header routing (mobile teams, SDKs). less accidental surface area. denylist gets big and brittle.

pj: big Q: telemetry. If we change ordering, our canary telemetry (p95/p99 by cohort) might get weird. we already see cardinality explosion with tenant+route+header combos

samira: correct — telemetry costs are the blocker. canary owners want cohort-level rollouts but not infinite metric series. proposal: sample 10% of header-based routed requests for full metric tagging; aggregate the rest into a single "header-routed:other" bucket.

ken: sample in the gateway or in the ingest pipeline? gateway saves us from sending extraneous tags, but we lose visibility if sampling logic is buggy.

eli: gateway. we include a signed sampling decision that downstream can verify. also emit a lightweight trace/event for sampled vs aggregated counts.

canary-bot: automatic note: new route-config schema v3.1 supports `headerRouting.allowlist` and `cohortSampling.rate` fields. see /docs/routing#v3.1 (placeholder link)

pj: UX: how will console show this? owners hate surprises when traffic isn't what they expect. Suggested UI: per-route traffic view with two panes: "deterministic split" and "header overrides". an inline indicator when header allowlist is active.

samira: add a live preview that evaluates a few example headers/ids and tells them target cohort. that helps customers validate rules without deploying.

eli: agreed. also add a warning if header allowlist + high sample rate would blow up metric cardinality. show estimated cost delta.

ken: edge-case: sticky cookie set by older infra will still route people into canary after header goes away. do we want TTL on cookie stickiness when header override was used?

eli: proposal: cookies set because of header override get a short TTL (e.g., 10m) unless the owner explicitly checks "promote header->sticky". default short TTL prevents long-term leakage.

pj: rollout policy: default canary split should be weight-based. header-based gets highest precedence only for allowlisted tenants and when the header is present AND non-empty. then cookie, then client-id hash. docs need exact precedence text.

samira: also a change to telemetry: add a new metric label `routing_source` with values: `weight`, `header`, `cookie`, `hash`, `aggregated-sampled`. that lets us roll up cost and quality by source. aggregated-sampled only present when we applied sampling.

ken: love that. how about quota enforcement? if header causes disproportionate canary traffic, we need route-level quota caps. e.g., header-routing cannot exceed X% of total route QPS unless owner overrides.

eli: make that part of the schema: `headerRouting.maxPercentOfRoute` and default to 20%. console should block save if you try to allow 100% without an enterprise flag.

pj: team ops: add an alert rule: if observed header-routed QPS > maxPercentOfRoute * routeQPS for >1m, fire warning. make it non-pager by default.

samira: testing: we need deterministic local harness change. the dev harness should let you fake headers and cookies and show the final evaluated cohort. we'll add a `--route-sim` flag to the CLI.

ken: compatibility: old route configs without headerRouting should behave exactly the same. new fields opt-in.

eli: ok next steps: write PR for gateway evaluator (small), consolidate telemetry sampling code with ingest team, wire up console preview + cost estimator. I'll draft a Proto change: `RouteConfig.v3_1` with fields: `headerRouting.allowlist (list of strings)`, `headerRouting.maxPercentOfRoute (int)`, `headerRouting.promoteSticky (bool)`, `cohortSampling.rate (float)`, `cookie.ttl_override_when_header (seconds)`.

pj: can you paste the proto sketch here when you have it? will review specifically for alerting labels.

eli: yup, end of day I can paste a diff. also proposing a small spike to measure metric cardinality when headerSampling is on — set up a week of shadow traffic to estimate.

samira: sounds good. :thumbsup:

ken: :+1:

pj: thanks everyone — this avoids a lot of accidental hijack cases we've seen.

canary-bot: Reminder: please add an owners field to RouteConfig when you open the PR so we can auto-create canary notifications.
